title: Looping over text
summary: Step through a string one character at a time to count letters or build new text.

intro.text:
A for loop can step through a string, **one character at a time**, from left to right:

```
for ch in "cat":
    print(ch)
```

prints c, a and t on separate lines. The **cells** panel points at the current character.

With this you can:

- **count** characters: a counter that grows when `ch` matches
- check if a character is one of several with `in`: `ch in "aeiou"` is True for a vowel
- **build** a new string: start with `""` and add to it each round

Strings never change. Building a new string means making a slightly longer one each round; the **history** panel shows every version.
intro.analogy: Reading a word letter by letter with your finger under each one, keeping a tally of the letters you care about on a sticky note as you go.

mistakes.title: Adding to a string that was never made
mistakes.explain: += needs a starting value. Start with out = "" before the loop.

mistakes.title: Adding a number to text
mistakes.explain: out is text and n is a number, so += cannot join them. Turn n into text with str().
